claims.claim: In an observational Italian study, about four in 100 people a year who stopped GLP-1 treatment had a non-fatal heart attack, stroke, or death, compared with about two in 100 who continued.
claims.episode_span: about four in 100 people a year who stopped a GLP-1 had a non-fatal heart attack, stroke, or death, roughly double the rate among people who stayed on treatment
claims.source_title: Stopping GLP-1 drugs could increase heart attack risk for some, study says
claims.supporting_quote: Researchers found four in every 100 of those people a year who stopped taking GLP-1 treatments had a non-fatal heart attack or stroke, or died, compared to about two in 100 of the people who stayed on the medication.

claims.claim: The study analysed 80,302 people with type 2 diabetes at 301 Italian clinics between 2004 and 2024 and was published in The Lancet Regional Health – Europe.
claims.episode_span: An observational analysis in The Lancet Regional Health – Europe, of 80,302 people with type 2 diabetes and no established cardiovascular disease seen at 301 Italian clinics from 2004 to 2024
claims.source_title: Stopping GLP-1 drugs linked to twice the risk of heart attack, stroke or death in people with diabetes
claims.supporting_quote: The study analysed health records of 80,302 people with type 2 diabetes who received care at 301 diabetes clinics across Italy between 2004 and 2024.

claims.claim: After matching, the combined outcome rate was 3.94 versus 1.96 events per 100 person-years, a hazard ratio of 2.03, in groups of 28,713.
claims.episode_span: each group had 28,713 people: the combined outcome occurred at 3.94 events per 100 person-years after discontinuation versus 1.96 among people who continued, a hazard ratio of 2.03
claims.source_title: Stopping GLP-1 drugs linked to twice the risk of heart attack, stroke or death in people with diabetes
claims.supporting_quote: The incidence of the combined cardiovascular and mortality outcome was 3.94 events per 100 person-years among those who discontinued treatment, compared with 1.96 events per 100 person-years among those who continued. This translated into a hazard ratio of 2.03

claims.claim: Death rates were 2.23 versus 0.48 per 100 person-years, with a hazard ratio of 4.81.
claims.episode_span: Death from any cause was 2.23 versus 0.48 events per 100 person-years, a hazard ratio of 4.81
claims.source_title: Stopping GLP-1 drugs linked to twice the risk of heart attack, stroke or death in people with diabetes
claims.supporting_quote: For death from any cause, the incidence was 2.23 events per 100 person-years in the discontinuation group, compared with 0.48 events per 100 person-years among those who continued treatment. The hazard ratio was 4.81.

claims.claim: About 60 percent stopped after about one year, while continuers stayed about three years, and the association was stronger at BMI 30 or above.
claims.episode_span: About 60 percent of starters stopped after about one year, while people who stayed on treatment did so for about three years.
claims.source_title: Stopping GLP-1 drugs could increase heart attack risk for some, study says
claims.supporting_quote: Of the more than 80,000 people who started GLP-1s, those who stayed on treatment did so for about three years. The group that did not stay on treatment, about 60 per cent, is reported to have stopped use after about one year.

claims.claim: A BMJ analysis cautioned the study could not show that discontinuation caused the higher risk, and did not analyze why people stopped.
claims.episode_span: The study cannot show that stopping caused the extra events: it did not establish why people stopped, including gastrointestinal effects, cost, or illness
claims.source_title: Stopping GLP-1 drugs could increase heart attack risk for some, study says
claims.supporting_quote: An analysis by the British Medical Journal notes the study could not determine if discontinuing GLP-1 drugs directly caused the increased risk, or if people who experienced a higher risk of health events were already in poorer health.

claims.claim: A review of 63 trials found average weight regain of 0.4 kilograms per month after stopping weight-loss drugs.
claims.episode_span: a separate review of 63 trials and more than 9,000 people, published in the BMJ in January 2026, found weight regain averaging 0.4 kilograms a month after weight-loss drugs were stopped
claims.source_title: Stopping GLP-1 drugs could increase heart attack risk for some, study says
claims.supporting_quote: A study published in the BMJ in January 2026 showed weight-loss drug users on average regain weight at a rate of 0.4 kilograms or 0.88 pounds per month after they stop. That study reviewed 63 trials covering more than 9,000 individuals up to February 2025.

claims.claim: The FDA required GLP-1 labels to warn of NAION, a rare optic-nerve condition that can cause permanent vision loss, naming Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound, and Soliqua.
claims.episode_span: warning that GLP-1 medicines may be associated with nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy
claims.source_title: GLP-1 Weight Loss Drug Side Effects Include Permanent Blindness, Warns FDA
claims.supporting_quote: The drug administration body clarified that the GLP-1 medications, including Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Wegovy, Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro and Zepbound, as well as Sanofi’s Soliqua need information about the potential risk of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy on warning labels.

claims.claim: MedStar emergency physician Miriam Fischer reported daily ER visits for severe GLP-1 gastrointestinal effects, dehydration, gallbladder problems, pancreatitis, and kidney stones, including among people using the drugs without supervision.
claims.episode_span: patients arrive every day with GLP-1 side effects, and that emergency physicians are seeing more preventable visits as people also buy these drugs online and use them without medical supervision
claims.source_title: ERs see surge in GLP-1 side effects | What to know
claims.supporting_quote: MedStar Health emergency medicine physician Dr. Miriam Fischer told WBAL-TV 11 News that patients arrive at the emergency room every day with side effects of GLP-1 medications.

claims.claim: In 49 women with lipoedema treated with tirzepatide, symptom change was not significantly associated with weight change, and every participant improved at least 30 percent on the QuASiL, but there was no control group.
claims.episode_span: Percentage weight change was not significantly associated with percentage symptom change (r = 0.058, p = 0.692)
claims.source_title: Symptom improvement was not significantly associated with weight loss, dose, or treatment duration in women with lipoedema treated with tirzepatide
claims.supporting_quote: Weight change was not significantly associated with symptom change (r = 0.058, 95% confidence interval -0.23 to 0.33; p = 0.692).

claims.claim: In 90 patients switched to tirzepatide, higher baseline monocyte GIPR mRNA was associated with greater weight and FIB-4 reductions, and native GIP suppressed LPS-induced IL-6 and TNF-alpha in monocytes ex vivo.
claims.episode_span: higher baseline monocyte GIP-receptor mRNA tracked with larger drops in body weight and in the fibrosis-4 index over six months after a switch to tirzepatide
claims.source_title: Baseline monocyte GIP receptor mRNA expression is associated with reductions in body weight and FIB-4 index after switching to tirzepatide
claims.supporting_quote: Higher baseline monocyte GIPR mRNA expression was associated with greater reductions in body weight and the FIB-4 index and remained significant in multivariable models.

claims.claim: Tirzepatide is approved for type 2 diabetes in the USA, Europe, and the UAE, and in SURPASS 1-5 reduced HbA1c by 1.24 to 2.58 percent and body weight by 5.4 to 11.7 kg, more than semaglutide or titrated basal insulin.
claims.episode_span: Five trials in people with type 2 diabetes found that tirzepatide reduced HbA1c by 1.24 to 2.58 percentage points and body weight by 5.4 to 11.7 kilograms
claims.source_title: Tirzepatide, a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor co-agonist for the treatment of type 2 diabetes
claims.supporting_quote: Five clinical trials in type 2-diabetic subjects (SURPASS 1-5) have shown that tirzepatide at 5-15 mg per week reduces both HbA1c (1.24 to 2.58%) and body weight (5.4-11.7 kg) by amounts unprecedented for a single agent.

claims.claim: A meta-analysis of seven trials and 6609 adults found dose-dependent HbA1c superiority for tirzepatide versus placebo, GLP-1 receptor agonists, and basal insulin, with more gastrointestinal events than placebo.
claims.episode_span: pooling seven randomized trials of at least 12 weeks in 6,609 adults with type 2 diabetes, found dose-dependent superiority on HbA1c
claims.source_title: Management of type 2 diabetes with the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims.supporting_quote: Seven trials (6609 participants) were included. A dose-dependent superiority in lowering HbA1c was evident with all three tirzepatide doses vs all comparators

claims.claim: Tirzepatide is a 39-amino-acid peptide based on native GIP, and co-infusion of GLP-1 and GIP was reported to increase insulin response and glucagon suppression compared with either hormone alone.
claims.episode_span: infusing GLP-1 and GIP together produced a larger insulin response and a stronger suppression of glucagon than giving either hormone alone
claims.source_title: The Role of Tirzepatide, Dual GIP and GLP-1 Receptor Agonist, in the Management of Type 2 Diabetes: The SURPASS Clinical Trials
claims.supporting_quote: emerging evidence has illustrated that co-infusion of GLP-1 and GIP has a synergetic effect, resulting in significantly increased insulin response and glucagonostatic response, compared with separate administration of each hormone.
